## Simple explanation

Runtime can mean the time a program is running or the software environment
that executes it. In AI systems, it may refer to a model-serving engine
that loads a model and handles inference requests.

## Technical explanation

The term has context-dependent meanings: execution time, a language
runtime, or an inference runtime that manages model execution, operators,
devices, and memory. Runtime behavior depends on the program, dependencies,
hardware, and configuration.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The runtime affects compatibility, performance, memory use, and operational
reliability. A model that trains successfully may still need conversion,
optimized kernels, or runtime-specific changes before deployment.

## How it works

A runtime loads code or a model artifact, resolves required operations,
allocates resources, and executes work. Inference runtimes may schedule
requests, select CPU/GPU kernels, batch inputs, and report errors or
performance metrics.

## Practical example

An engineer can export a trained model and load it with an inference
runtime on a target device. They should verify numerical agreement and
measure end-to-end latency and memory use with representative inputs.

## Common misconceptions

- Runtime is not always synonymous with execution speed; it can refer to
  the software environment itself.
- A faster benchmark for one operation does not guarantee lower
  end-to-end application latency.
